thread:
elen.k (Support): Opening escalation for tenant "NovaPay" — they reported a regression in p95/p99 for requests that use tool routing + strict structured output. Baseline p95 ~220ms -> observed ~1.3s after the schema/router changes last night. Ticket S-3612.

ryan.m (Eng Runtime): Thanks. Any traces or example payloads? specifically want to know if they use many distinct schemas or remote $ref trees.

elen.k (Support): They've attached an example and trace id: rw-c9d2ff. Payload uses three tool calls (lookup_account, format_receipt, notify) and a structured schema with nested $refs. They set "validate_mode": "strict".

elen.k (Support): ```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "rwd-infer-1-medium",
  "prompt": "assemble receipt and call tools",
  "tool_calls": ["lookup_account","format_receipt","notify"],
  "structured_output": {
    "schema": {"$ref": "https://schemas.novapay.com/receipt-v3.json"},
    "validate_mode": "strict"
  },
  "options": {"timeout_ms": 45000}
}
```

parul.d (SRE): I pulled the rw-c9d2ff trace. Breakdown from router spans: ingress->router 260ms, router->model 310ms, but validator.compile_and_run 850ms on p95 and ~1.5s on p99. Router hosts showed short-lived user-space CPU spikes pinned to validation threads.

ashok.v (Platform): We merged a change in tool-router v1.10 to fetch remote $refs and inline them before validation. That code path intentionally resolves refs synchronously; if a ref was uncached we hit I/O + compile inside the request. Not great.

ryan.m (Eng Runtime): If compile happens on the request thread, AJV and similar validators can be costly for deep refs. Repro steps? can someone replay the exact payload?

parul.d (SRE): I replayed it in staging. Cold run where refs weren't cached: compile 780-950ms, validation 40-60ms. Warm runs: compile is essentially zero with cache and validation 30-80ms. So p99 is driven by cold compiles and remote fetch latency.

elen.k (Support): Customer says their traffic is spiky and uses many receipt variants (so many unique schema combinations). They can't tolerate cold-compile tail.

ashok.v (Platform): Immediate mitigations we can offer: 1) tenant header to disable strict validation (X-RW-Validate: lax) as a temporary escape hatch; 2) hotfix: shared in-process compile cache with a small LRU + shared memory ipc between router workers; 3) CDN artifact + prefetch for tenant-uploaded schemas.

ops-bot: deploy: tool-router hotfix (schema-cache-shm) scheduled -> canary on 2 hosts.

ryan.m (Eng Runtime): Longer term fixes I'm proposing: - precompile on route registration (when customer binds tools/schemas), - offload compile to background compiler pool (Rust/wasm workers) so request thread only waits on a fast compiled validator handle, - or use a lightweight WASM-based validator compiled ahead-of-time for complex schemas.

parul.d (SRE): I agree. For now, I've enabled tenant bypass for NovaPay and started the canary. Telemetry after bypass: p95 dropped from 1.3s -> 290ms; p99 to ~430ms. CPU on router reduced.

ops-bot: canary result: success (2/2) -> rolling to rest of fleet (10 hosts).

elen.k (Support): NovaPay confirmed improvement and is okay with temporary bypass if we give ETA for durable fix. They uploaded their schema bundle to our artifact-uploads S3 path per our instructions.

ryan.m (Eng Runtime): I'll work on two PRs: 1) shared compile cache (LRU+shm) that's feature-flagged; 2) background compiler service that subscribes to schema-upload events and precompiles validators. Do we have an event pipeline for artifact uploads?

ashok.v (Platform): Yes, artifact uploads send events to schema-indexer topic. We'll extend indexer to enqueue precompile jobs. Also planning CDN hosting for common refs.

parul.d (SRE): Post-incident monitoring: add schema_compile_time histogram metric, schema_cache_hit_rate gauge, and an alert when tenant p95 increases >300ms above baseline for any schema-validating route.

ryan.m (Eng Runtime): Quick bench notes I ran: ajv.compile for NovaPay top-level schema (8 remote refs) cold ~920ms, warm ~75ms. Moving compile to a background worker reduces tail because first request can wait on a warm handle or fallback to lax. WASM experiments show ~200ms cold but ~15-30ms warm; still worth investigating.

ops-bot: PR opened: redwood/tool-router#4012 (shm-compile-cache + metrics) -> CI passing.

elen.k (Support): Customer asks if we can pre-warm validators for the first hour after upload. Is that doable?

ryan.m (Eng Runtime): Yes — indexer can enqueue prewarm jobs on upload, and the compiler pool will compile and populate the cache. ETA: cache hotfix in 48h, compiler pool + prewarm in ~2 weeks. I'll include a tenant opt-in header for prewarm.

parul.d (SRE): I'll draft the postmortem and link trace rw-c9d2ff and ticket S-3612. Also adding dashboards showing schema_compile_ms per-tenant.

ashok.v (Platform): Rolling feature flag so we can enable shm-cache per-tenant. Also adding a fallback policy: if compile_time > 400ms we will fail-open to lax validation for that request and emit an incident event.

ops-bot: rollout: schema-cache-shm deployed -> success (all hosts).

elen.k (Support): Customer validated after the shard deploy: p95 ~300ms, p99 ~460ms over last 30m. They're relieved and will monitor 48h. They requested a firm ETA for the precompile flow.

ryan.m (Eng Runtime): RFC/plan assigned. Action items: Ryan -> finish compiler-pool PR; Ashok -> implement prewarm trigger in indexer; Parul -> postmortem + alerts; Elen -> customer comms.

elen.k (Support): I'll keep customer posted. Closing interim escalation once RFC dates are confirmed. Thanks team :white_check_mark:
